'''Hypnotic Brass Ensemble''' is an eight-piece, Chicago-based brass ensemble consisting of eight sons of the jazz trumpeter [[Phil Cohran]].<ref name=":0" /> Their musical style ranges from [[Hip hop music|hip hop]] to [[jazz]] to [[funk]] and [[Rock music|rock]], including [[calypso music|calypso]] and [[Romani people|gypsy]] music. They call their eclectic blend of sound "now music", or "Hypnotic". Reared in the teachings of [[music]] since they were children, they grew up on the stage playing as the "Phil Cohran Youth Ensemble".

==Early history==
The brothers were raised in a house where music was a constant element of the household. [[Phil Cohran]]'s "Circle of Sound" held rehearsals in the living room and put on live shows in the adjacent loft/theatre called the "Sun Ark". The brothers were obligated to wake at 6am  and play their horns before and after school. As adolescents, they played around [[Chicago]] as the '''Phil Cohran Youth Ensemble''', performing for the likes of [[Harold Washington]], [[Nelson Mandela]], and other prominent figures of the day.

As the brothers grew into high school, many of them set their horns aside for a while. Enduring the deaths of close friends and family, including brother Anthony Neal, close friend Robert Lock (for whom they later wrote a song entitled "Flipside"), and Level Todd (for whom their song "Todd" was written), they decided to pick their horns back up. In 1999, the brothers took to the subways of Chicago and presented their music. Shortly after, they formed a fully-fledged, eight-piece brass ensemble and by 2004 recorded their first project, ''Flipside''.<ref>{{cite web|title=Interview: Hypnotic Brass Ensemble|url=http://venueone.com/#!/blog/interview-hypnotic-brass-ensemble/|publisher=VenueOne|accessdate=September 7, 2012}}</ref> They moved to [[New York City]] in 2006.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |last=Cardy |first=Tom |date=2012-07-18 |title=Hypnotic Brass Ensemble psyched for Wellington |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/dominion-post/culture/7303879/Hypnotic-Brass-Ensemble-psyched-for-Wellington |access-date=2023-11-26 |newspaper=[[The Post (New Zealand newspaper)|The Dominion Post]] |publisher=[[Stuff (company)|Stuff Ltd]] }}</ref>{{page needed|date=November 2023}}

==Collaborations==
They have performed with [[Mos Def]], Aquilla Sadalla,  [[Phil Cohran]], [[The Recipe (band)|The Recipe]], Nomadic Massive, [[Tony Allen (musician)|Tony Allen]], [[Wu Tang Clan]], [[De La Soul]], [[Prince (musician)|Prince]], [[Femi Kuti]], [[Gorillaz]], [[The B-52's]], and at the [[North Sea Jazz Festival]]. They have recorded with names ranging from [[Snoop Dogg]], Ben Billions [[Erykah Badu]] to [[RZA]] and [[Ghostface Killah]] of the [[Wu Tang Clan]] to [[BK-One]] to [[Childish Gambino]] to [[Maxwell (musician)|Maxwell]]. They supported [[Blur (band)|Blur]] for their Hyde Park reunion concerts on 2–3 July 2009. They are also collaborators on a number of tracks from the third [[Gorillaz]] studio album, ''[[Plastic Beach#Personnel|Plastic Beach]]''.<ref>{{cite AV media notes |title=Plastic Beach |type=Experience Edition liner notes |author=[[Gorillaz]] |publisher=[[Parlophone]] |year=2010 |id=5099962616720}}</ref>

One of their songs "War" was featured in the box office smash film ''[[The Hunger Games (film)|The Hunger Games]]'' as the theme song for the in-universe eponymous sport hosted by [[List of The Hunger Games characters#Caesar Flickerman|Caesar Flickerman]],<ref name=":0" />{{page needed|date=November 2023}} and on the soundtrack for [[Fargo (season 4)|season 4]] of ''[[Fargo (TV series)|Fargo]].'' It was sampled in "American Royalty" by Childish Gambino featuring RZA in the former's 2012 mixtape ''[[Royalty (mixtape)|Royalty]]''. They collaborated on tracks with the group [[Rocket Juice & the Moon]], a project featuring [[Damon Albarn]] (Blur, Gorillaz) on vocals/guitar/keyboard, [[Flea (musician)|Flea]] ([[Red Hot Chili Peppers]]) on bass, and legendary Afrobeat drummer [[Tony Allen (musician)|Tony Allen]] ([[Fela Kuti]] and many others) on the group's self-titled debut album. As part of independent label Jagjaguwar's 25th anniversary, the group performed a reimagined version of ''Sapphie'' by [[Richard Youngs]] alongside [[Moses Sumney]], [[Perfume Genius]], and [[Sharon Van Etten]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://shorefire.com/releases/entry/jagjaguwar-launches-second-installment-in-year-long-25th-anniversary-celebration-with-this-is-a-mindfulness-drill|title=Jagjaguwar Launches Second Installment in Year-Long 25th Anniversary Celebration with This is a Mindfulness Drill}}</ref>
